blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — adult azithromycin dosing for mild community-acquired pneumonia
stem: An adult is prescribed oral azithromycin for mild community-acquired pneumonia using the labeled 5-day regimen. Which schedule matches the prescribing information?

options.A: Take 500 mg as a single dose on day 1, then take 250 mg once daily on days 2 through 5 to complete the labeled course.
options.B: Take 250 mg once daily on days 1 through 5, using the same dose each day because no loading dose is included in the labeled course.
options.C: Take 500 mg once daily on days 1 through 5, maintaining the initial dose throughout the entire labeled treatment course.
options.D: Take 250 mg on day 1 and increase to 500 mg once daily on days 2 through 5 so exposure rises during the remainder of treatment.

rationale: Current azithromycin tablet prescribing information lists, for adult community-acquired pneumonia of mild severity, 500 mg as a single dose on day 1 followed by 250 mg once daily on days 2 through 5. Therefore A is correct. B omits the labeled 500-mg day-1 dose, C uses 500 mg for too many days, and D reverses the labeled loading/maintenance pattern.
educational_objective: Identify the labeled adult 5-day oral azithromycin regimen for mild community-acquired pneumonia as 500 mg on day 1 followed by 250 mg once daily on days 2 through 5.
